customManagers.description: The mise manager does not support the dotnet tool. Track its SDK pin alongside global.json so both declarations move together.
Track the bundled Myriad host pins with the generator packages.
Track the Myriad.Core version embedded in the plugin scaffold's project template.

packageRules.description: Group build and documentation tooling together, following morphir-rust. Major tooling updates stay separate from non-major updates.
Group NuGet patches across centrally managed packages and dotnet tools. Keep them separate from minor upgrades that may need code changes.
Group NuGet minor updates separately from patches. Major NuGet upgrades retain the recommended per-package or related-package groups.
Group Rust plugin patch updates separately from minor and major updates.
Group Rust plugin minor updates separately; pre-1.0 minor releases can be breaking changes.
Group Rust plugin major updates separately from non-major updates.

Update global.json and mise.toml SDK pins together on the .NET 11 SDK. Libraries also target .NET 10 LTS through MorphirLibraryTargetFrameworks in Directory.Build.props. Review the next SDK major explicitly.
Keep the development-container SDK on the same .NET 11 SDK baseline and in the same update PR as global.json and mise.toml.
The development container copies the .NET 10 shared runtime, so the tests can run the net10.0 consumers of the library packages. Keep this image on .NET 10.

The MSBuild tasks target net10.0 and load into the MSBuild of the .NET 10 SDK. Microsoft.Build.* 18.1 and later ship only net11.0 and net472 assets. Keep the 18.0 line until the tasks move to a newer hosted target framework.
Shouldly.Json minor releases can require major JSON library upgrades. Update the assertion helper and JSON libraries together, and review schema validation compatibility before merging.

Myriad's host, plugins and generator contract share Fantomas AST types. Fabulous.AST also requires an exact Fantomas.Core version. Update this code generation toolchain independently of general NuGet updates and review host/runtime compatibility before merging.

FSharp.Compiler.Service requires one exact FSharp.Core version, and the F# frontend evidence depends on the compiler. Update them together, and review the FSharp.Core version that the new compiler service requires before merging. Rerun the F# frontend tests on every compiler update.

Verify.TUnit can raise its TUnit.Core minimum in a patch release. Update TUnit, Verify, Reqnroll and their testing-platform dependencies together so the engine, generators and runtime stay compatible, even when their update types differ.
